meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'говаривать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'persuade'.

examples.text: Не уговаривай меня остаться здесь, в тепле.
examples.trans: Do not persuade me to stay here in the warmth.

examples.text: Да не буду я её уговаривать.
examples.trans: I am not going to persuade her.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'they', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to become', paired with 'становиться'.

examples.text: Ты слишком сентиментальным стал. А лидер должен быть жёстким.
examples.trans: You've become too sentimental. And a leader has to be tough.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'вежий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fresh').

examples.text: Свежие ягоды, кофе! У вас тут романтический завтрак.
examples.trans: Fresh berries, coffee! You are having a romantic breakfast here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'shop, store' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: What to do? Let's go to the shop.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to buy', paired with 'покупать'.

examples.text: Юле бы дублёнку купили, Славику бы ноутбук.
examples.trans: We could have bought Yulia a sheepskin coat, and Slavik a laptop.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'таричок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'old buddy, old fellow' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a old buddy, old fellow.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('golden, gold').

examples.trans: He's very good with his hands.

examples.text: Товарищ генерал, операция называется Золотой ярд.
examples.trans: Comrade General, the operation is called Golden Yard.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('familiar, known').

examples.text: А знакомо ли тебе, Аркашка, слово педикюр?
examples.trans: And are you familiar, Arkashka, with the word pedicure?

examples.text: Я услышал в коридоре знакомый голос.
examples.trans: I heard a familiar voice in the corridor.
I will call acquaintances right now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'огнать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'drove up'.

examples.text: Ты дашь охраннику, чтобы через полчаса подогнал к веранде.
examples.trans: You will give them to the guard so he drives it up to the terrace in half an hour.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и подогнать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and drove up on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'five', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы же только начинаем. Через месяц будет пять тысяч.
examples.trans: But we're only just starting. In a month there'll be five thousand.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'time, occasion' in everyday Russian.
High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'cheaper', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It is cheaper to find new people.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'no ... at all, not any', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I have no money at all.

examples.text: Да нет у тебя никаких денег.
examples.trans: But you don't have any money.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'двох'). Common masculine noun meaning 'catch, trick' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новый подвох.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new catch.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('normal').
Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('honest').

examples.text: Я ухожу. Ваш сын будет бедным и честным.
examples.trans: I'm leaving. Your son will be poor and honest.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'contraband, smuggled goods' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Are you offering me contraband again?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'прос'). Common masculine noun meaning 'question; matter' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'shark' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: She circled around me like a shark.

examples.text: Это она со мной познакомилась! Ходила вокруг меня, как акула.
examples.trans: She was the one who met me! She circled around me like a shark.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('necessary, needed').

Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ймать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to catch', paired with 'ловить'.

examples.text: Ты бандитов поймал! Которые банкомат на Гарибальди ограбили.
examples.trans: You caught bandits! Who robbed the ATM on Garibaldi Street.

посадить.gloss: to seat; to plant; to put in prison

meanings.en: to seat; to plant; to put in prison
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'садить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to seat; to plant; to put in prison', paired with 'сажать'.

examples.text: Аникеев? Ну что, проворовался? Да я тебя посажу!
examples.trans: Anikeev? Well then, caught stealing? I'll put you in prison!
